title: Real-Time Stock Market Data Platform & Alert Engine with Python, Kafka, TimescaleDB & Redis
problem: Retail investors and quantitative traders miss lucrative market opportunities and risk severe losses during flash crashes when trading platforms suffer from delayed quote updates, sluggish chart rendering, and unresponsive price alerts. Polling relational databases for market ticks introduces multi-second staleness and database lock contention under high-frequency tick volume. This project builds a production-grade real-time stock market data platform and alert engine in Python. The system ingests streaming trade ticks over Apache Kafka at 10,000+ ticks per second, generates 1-minute and 5-minute OHLCV candlestick bars in TimescaleDB hypertables, caches live ticker prices and trigger thresholds in Redis, evaluates dynamic price alerts with sub-12ms latency, and streams real-time market updates to React trading dashboards over WebSockets.

use_cases.title: Algorithmic Day-Trading Price Spike Alerts
use_cases.first_sentence: Active day traders monitoring volatile equities need instant notifications when a stock crosses a moving average or breaks out of a price range.
use_cases.second_sentence: The alert engine evaluates incoming price ticks against Redis threshold sets in memory, pushing an alert to the trader's dashboard within 10 milliseconds of trigger.

use_cases.title: Real-Time Multi-Asset Portfolio Valuation
use_cases.first_sentence: FinTech investment platforms managing customer equity portfolios require continuous net asset value (NAV) recalculations as asset prices fluctuate.
use_cases.second_sentence: The system streams live price ticks over WebSockets, updating portfolio valuation totals and sector allocation charts in real time without screen reloads.

use_cases.title: Quantitative Backtesting & Historical OHLCV Analysis
use_cases.first_sentence: Quantitative analysts designing automated trading strategies need fast access to historical multi-year candlestick bars for technical indicator calculations.
use_cases.second_sentence: TimescaleDB continuous aggregates compute rolling 1-minute and 1-hour OHLCV candles, serving multi-year chart lookups in sub-30ms analytical query response times.

hard_parts: Ingesting and aggregating high-velocity market tick streams in Kafka into 1-minute OHLCV candlestick bars without dropping out-of-order ticks
Designing TimescaleDB hypertables with optimal chunk time intervals and continuous aggregate policies for fast analytical charting
Evaluating thousands of active user price threshold alerts in Redis using sorted sets (ZREVRANGEBYSCORE) with sub-12ms evaluation latency
Streaming real-time ticker quotes and candlestick updates over WebSockets to React trading dashboards with zero UI jank
screener_signals: Clean Python codebase cleanly separating Kafka tick consumers, TimescaleDB hypertable managers, Redis alert engines, and WebSocket push services
Throughput benchmark proving sustained ingestion of 10,000+ market ticks per second with sub-12ms alert evaluation latency
Anti-fake verification script setting an alert for 'AAPL >= 195.00', emitting a synthetic Kafka tick for AAPL at $195.50, and asserting the alert trigger notification fires in under 50 milliseconds

architecture.data_flow: Market data sources publish trade ticks to the Kafka 'stock-ticks' topic; the Python streaming worker consumes ticks, updates the latest price in Redis, and pushes price updates to the WebSocket gateway; the alert engine queries Redis sorted sets to identify triggered price alerts and emits alert events; simultaneously, the worker aggregates ticks into 1-minute OHLCV candlestick records and batches inserts into TimescaleDB; connected React clients receive real-time ticker updates over WebSockets, re-rendering candlestick charts and displaying alert notification modals; historical chart requests query TimescaleDB continuous aggregates via REST API.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Redis sorted set atomic score lookups preventing missed alert triggers; TimescaleDB hypertable constraints enforcing trade time validity.

prerequisites: Proficiency in Python asynchronous programming, streaming architectures (Kafka), and database interactions
Understanding of time-series databases (TimescaleDB / PostgreSQL), in-memory caching (Redis), and WebSocket streaming

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU, network, and storage I/O bound data pipeline software)
environment.cost: $0 (fully open-source stack using local Docker Desktop for Kafka, TimescaleDB, and Redis)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or real stock brokerage API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Docker Desktop (Kafka, TimescaleDB, and Redis containers) and Python 3.11+
environment.fallback_path: In-memory Python queue and SQLite database fallback if Docker containers are unavailable

riskiest_component.name: TimescaleDB Write Amplification and Alert Trigger Stampedes
riskiest_component.mitigation: Buffer tick insertions in memory and execute bulk COPY commands into TimescaleDB, and rate-limit duplicate alert notifications.
riskiest_component.fallback: Tiered downsampling aggregating ticks into 5-second summary batches before database persistence.
